frames.review_note: Minor only. Nagoji's collar ring hangs at the front, not the side. His tunic drapes as ragged sleeve cloth over both arms, which reads a little sleeved but keeps the left forearm covered as required. His eyes are fully closed, not half closed. The pen chain runs fairly taut at chest height between the collars instead of drooping onto the plank. The faces, irons, closed hold with lantern glow, Nagoji left and Keshavrao right, and Keshavrao's lock (young, faint moustache, ragged short hair, grey-brown tunic, no stud, thin unbandaged hands) all match. The upper-right wall suits the balloon and the bottom strip over the knees suits the caption. v02 is the same art with no pen chain and a bare left forearm. v01 is rejected: it is set on an open deck in rain with red-waistcoated guards.

Minor. The guard's raised hand grips the edge of the canvas awning, not the hatch frame. Besides the cross-belt he wears a narrow waist belt (not wide, and no key ring). Faint plank highlights at the far left (about x 0.01 to 0.07, y 0.49 to 0.54) could suggest stencil marks at a squint, but a contrast check shows wood grain, not letterforms. The guard look matches: lean, dark-bearded, steel morion, soaked buff jerkin with cross-belt over a shirt, flintlock in hand, rain pouring through the hatch as the awning is dragged across. v01 is preferred: its small top-left box sits on dark beams clear of the musket hand, while v02's tall left box reaches down to the hand gripping the musket.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Minor only. The ladder is not in frame; the musket lies by the right-hand post, so 'near the foot of the ladder' is implied rather than shown (2.4 shows the ladder). The background prisoners look toward the camera and foreground rather than plainly at the musket, but Nagoji and Keshavrao both look down-right at it. The irons match 1.2: collar-to-collar pen chain through side rings, bandaged wrists under manacles, hobble chains. Nagoji's left forearm is covered by bandage and an ochre flap. Captions go in the top band: beams above the heads, with the right half fully clear. Rejected: v02 (no collars), v03 (no musket), v06 (a deck scene in daylight with a guard). v05, v07 and v08 have Nagoji gazing up and away from the musket. v04 has Keshavrao's second wrist apparently unmanacled and oversized dangling chains. Backup v01 stages the beat best (ladder, beam, every head turned) but has no collar-to-collar pen chain, so it matches 1.2 and 2.3 less well.

Clean. The guard is seen from behind in a morion and buff jerkin with cross-belt, silhouetted in the open hatch against rain and storm light, head turned toward the deck, never looking down. The painted balloons have long tails, but both point at the guard (the correct speaker), and the drawn balloons will cover them. The frame is 2.65:1 and the slot is about 3.97:1, so set visible_rect to roughly [0,0,2043,515] to keep the hatch, guard and beams without letterboxing. v05 is the same art pre-letterboxed to a 5.35:1 strip, which the contain fit would place thinner than the slot. v02 is an outdoor fort scene (reject). v03 and v04 are acceptable but have oversized painted balloons.

Framing is a medium-wide two-shot rather than a 'close' one, which suits the 2.53:1 strip. Keshavrao's eyes are downcast toward the floor, slightly screen-left, rather than clearly toward the musket (screen-right in 2.1). The seawater reads as a wet sheen on the boards rather than a visible threading current. Identity and irons are correct: Nagoji on the left with clean chin, curled moustache, stud, bandaged wrists and left forearm covered; Keshavrao on the right; pen chain collar to collar. Nagoji looks up at the lit hatch stairwell, where rain comes down as in 1.5. v01, v03 and v04 drop Nagoji's wrist bandages, run a chain from collar to wrists, and are 1.5:1, needing a heavy crop. v02 puts an armed guard in the hold (reject).

Minor. The floor carries a shallow sheet of water, and water cascades down the ladder steps, rather than a single thin thread (it matches the 2.3 stairwell). The current does curl around the stock. The flintlock (cock and frizzen visible) lies against the beam, and the ladder rises into grey storm light. The visible strip (y 187-575) is exactly the 5.09:1 slot, with a clear caption band over the dark beams at upper left. v04 is the same art full-frame; it needs a crop to about [0,245,1959,630] and would lose most of the sky. v01 is also acceptable, but its current runs by the barrel rather than the stock, and it needs a heavy crop. v02 is an unrelated scene (reject).

Minor only. A thin black frame border and white margin are painted inside the image (crop them at placement). Nagoji's wrist chain runs longer than a forearm and meets his collar chain near Keshavrao's cuff. There is a small pale window-like patch at the extreme top-left edge. Otherwise sound: the lantern-lit hold matches pages 2 and 3. Nagoji is on the left (thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud, ochre rags) and clamps his bandaged hand on Keshavrao's forearm, with the inner forearm turned from camera. Keshavrao is on the right (ragged short hair, faint moustache, grey-brown rags, collar with the side pen chain, bare hands), sliding away and reaching for a barrel. The chain meets his cuff. There is no text, and the panel is silent as the script calls for. Rejected: v02 and v03 show Keshavrao with no iron collar, and v03 also has a bright storm window. v04 puts Nagoji in a white tunic with a red sash. v01 is on the open deck with guards and sky.

v02 is acceptable. The camera looks straight up at the underside of the deck at the moment of impact. The planks bow downward, and sheets of water and grit pour through the seams while the beams and hull timbers stay whole. There are no figures, no text, no sky and no open hatch. The painted blank balloons sit upper left (before the impact) and lower right (after it), with no tails. That is right, because both speakers are sailors off panel above the deck. Both balloons bleed off the frame edges, but the letterer covers them. v01 is rejected: its painted balloon tails point at men in the hold instead of off-panel sailors, the ceiling shows bright openings, and it adds figures the script does not call for.

v02 is acceptable. It shows the ring bolted under the overhead beam, cracks and lifting splinters around the plate, and the chain rising at a slant from out of frame lower left, inside a lantern-lit hold that matches 4.5 and 5.2. Minor points: the plate uses crisp hexagonal nuts that look slightly machine-made, the chain is heavier than the collar chain in neighbouring panels, and the hold looks dry here. The painted box upper left sits over plain beam and gets covered. v01 is rejected because it is set outdoors in daylight with palm trees and a stockade fence, so it is not the closed hold.

v06 is acceptable. The ring hangs from one bolt in a freshly splintered beam, and its chain drops slack into the water at the far end of the row. The row of collared, manacled prisoners is dragged sideways and leans to the left. Nagoji (front left) matches his sheet: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, bandaged hands, hinged collar. Keshavrao (second) matches his. Water pours through the deck seams, and the hull timbers stay whole, as 4.4 requires. The caption box upper left covers only ceiling. The backup v04 is weaker because the ring chain runs taut at a diagonal instead of sagging into the water. v05 is rejected because the hull is smashed open to the sea and rain at right, which breaks 4.4. v03 is rejected because the ring hangs detached from the chain, which anticipates 5.5. v02 is rejected because the lead prisoner is a bearded curly-haired man who reads as a bearded Nagoji, and nobody wears collars. v01 is rejected because it is set outside the ship on open sea with guards on deck.

v04 is acceptable. Nagoji (left) and Keshavrao (right) grip the chain in manacled fists and haul it level toward the camera, feet braced in the flood water. The ring hangs from the beam by a single bolt, and its chain drops behind them without attaching to either collar, so nothing pulls on a neck. Nagoji has the moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud and bandaged wrists. Keshavrao has short hacked hair, a faint moustache and no stud. Both painted balloons sit at upper left over background with tails toward Nagoji, the correct speaker. Minor point: the beam around the ring is not visibly splintered as it was in 5.2. The backup v05 is almost identical, with the second painted balloon over the upper-right background. v06, v07, v08 and v09 are rejected because the ring chain runs down in a V into the collar chain between the two men, so it reads as hanging from their necks. v09 also has a long painted tail across the art. v02 and v03 are rejected because the floor is dry and the ring is bolted to the deck in the foreground, not in the beam. v01 is rejected because it is outdoors in daylight with guards.

v03 is acceptable. The freed chain whips away through a splash in the water between the two men, who stagger apart and look up into the open space overhead. Each still wears an empty hinged collar and wrist cuffs, and the ankle hobble chains are visible above the shallow water. Nagoji matches his sheet (moustache, clean chin, small ear stud, bandaged hands), and his left forearm is covered by the ochre sleeve, so the brand stays hidden. Keshavrao matches his sheet, with no stud. The wide frame suits the full-width row, and the lantern-lit hold matches 5.4. Minor points: Nagoji's wrist chain shows as short lengths hanging from each cuff, the tearing-out of the bolt is not shown, and Keshavrao has a bandage on one hand. The backup v04 (v05 is almost identical) shows deeper water that hides the hobbles, and the chain lies still instead of whipping. v02 works but is a 3:2 frame that would crop badly into a full-width row. v01 is rejected because its four painted boxes would stay blank in a panel with no text, the water is only a shallow puddle, and the empty rings are still bolted to the post.

Minor issues only. The 'its men stare after them' beat is implied rather than staged, because the background prisoners are still bent over their own rings. Nagoji's collar ring sits at the front rather than the side. Everything else matches: both men wear empty collars, manacles and hobbles; Nagoji has his ear stud and a clean chin, and his left forearm is wrapped; the hold is flooded and lantern-lit. There is clear space for balloons over the top-left background and for captions over the water. The v04 and v05 frames are pixel-identical. v01 and v02 were rejected: the floor is dry and no other prisoners are present. v06 was not chosen: its long painted tails cut across Nagoji's head.

Acceptable with a small setting quibble: behind the water is a wooden plank rim that reads a little like a trough edge, and his dhoti looks dry above the waterline, although 6.2 has him thigh-deep. In a tight insert with the bottom caption over most of the water, this reads well enough. v03 shows the lock best: the frizzen stands open above a dry, empty pan. The bandaged, manacled hands grip soundly and the forearms are covered or out of frame. v01 was rejected: Nagoji crouches dry beside a tub with his feet out of the water, contradicting the flooded hold, and his left forearm is bare and exposed.

v02 is the pick. It gives the high angle down the hatch at Keshavrao, and he matches his sheet: short ragged hair, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, wide eyes. He wears the iron collar with its side ring, his manacled hands grip the top, and his hobbled bare ankles are chained on a rung below. The painted balloon at top right has no tail, and sky and hatch give room for lettering. Minor points: the shaft is lit warm from below rather than by lightning, and the wrist chain is only visible dangling from one cuff. v01 is the same image without the iron collar, which the script requires, so it is rejected.

v08 is the pick. Nagoji is small in the mid-foreground, seen from behind, braced at the rail. His iron collar has the ring at the side, and his visible right wrist is manacled, chained and bandaged, with the left forearm hidden. A lightning-lit wave rears above the ship. The two insets along the bottom show Keshavrao's manacled hands clamped on the hatch rim with the chain between them, and a shattered spar in the sea. The crew have their backs to him. The painted boxes sit over sky and wave crest, clear of faces. Minor points: the sails look intact, whereas 8.1 has a snapped mainmast. One foreground sailor wears a tricorn and waistcoat, which fits the period but is not the head cloths of 8.1. The spar inset does not show the ship's side. v07 and v06 are the same art without the bandage on his hand. v01 to v05 draw Nagoji large, not small, and show Keshavrao's face in the inset instead of just his hands. In v01 a painted box also covers Keshavrao's eyes.

This is the only candidate, and it is usable. The wave crest breaks over the ship's rail and fills the frame, with no figures, no text and no anachronism. Weak points: the frame is 3:2 rather than a narrow strip, so it needs a horizontal crop through the middle band (rail plus curling water). The rail is a light open balustrade rather than the dark solid bulwark of 8.3. The sky is greyer and lighter than the night storm of 8.1 and 8.3, though it can pass as a lightning flash.

Minor issues only. v05 and v06 are the same art; only the size of the painted reserves differs. Nagoji matches his sheet and the chapter 3 row: thick curled moustache, clean chin, small gold ear stud, long curly hair, collar with side ring, bandaged manacled wrists, ankle irons with hobble chain, torn ochre tunic. His arms are extended at the end of the throw rather than mid-heave, so it reads a little like holding the rope. The rope lies short, halfway across, with coils on the wet deck and water pouring off at the scuppers on the right. Keshavrao (collar, manacles, faint moustache, grey-brown tunic, cream dhoti) is already fully out on the deck in front of a raised hatch coaming. In 9.3 he is back half inside the hatch. Each wrist chain dangles from its own cuff rather than visibly linking the pair, and Nagoji's long ochre tunic hem covers most of the cream dhoti. Hands are sound, and there is no text, gore or anachronism. Lettering: the caption goes in the upper left over the storm sky. Nagoji's balloon fits best in the sky and rigging at top centre, between his head and the mast, with its tail to his mouth. The painted box at the lower right will be covered.

Minor issues only. Keshavrao is half out of the hatch with the rope looped in his manacled hands, and the short wrist chain is caught across the rope. He has the collar with its side ring, faint moustache, short hair and grey-brown tunic, and his hands are sound. The rope runs back across the deck to Nagoji's bandaged, manacled hands at the left edge, and the next wave rears on the right with its white edge curling toward the hatch. Nagoji is cut off at the nose by the top edge, so the ear stud is out of frame. Moustache, light stubble and a clean chin show. His ochre cloth drapes over his forearms like sleeves (this keeps the left forearm covered), and Keshavrao's tunic droops over his left upper arm. There is no text and no noose: the loop is at his chest, not his neck. Rejected: v01 (3:2) and v03 have no collar on Keshavrao. v02 has no collar and paints a panel border inside the image, with dark cloud bands above and below.

Minor issues only. This is a medium shot rather than a true wide. The plunging bow is implied by the grey and white wave filling the background rather than drawn. His shin and raised knee rest over and among the coil rather than pressing squarely on it. Nagoji matches: thick curled moustache, clean chin with light captivity stubble, gold ear stud, empty collar with side ring, bandaged manacled hands with the chain sagging between the wrists, and a cream dhoti. The ochre drape covers the far (left) forearm. The rope runs dead straight and taut to the right, into the white water. The two caption reserves sit top-left and top-right, clear of his face and hands. Backup v02 is a truer wide: a sleeveless tunic per the sheet, his dhoti knee on the coil, the ankle cuff with hobble chain, and a better 3:1 aspect. But his left forearm is bare from elbow to cuff (outer side toward camera), so it is weaker on the brand-concealment rule. Rejected: v06 has no collar and the rope wraps a bitt. v07 runs a chain from the collar ring to the manacles, so the collar is not empty. v04 and v05 show hands only, with no knee or coil. v03 has no coil. v01 has a 2:1 frame and is weaker.

Minor issues only. The bandages are stripped into long trailing strips but not visibly scorched, and the palms are only mildly reddened. There is no torn flesh and no blood. Both open palms face the viewer with thumbs to the viewer's right, so the handedness is slightly ambiguous, but it reads naturally at print size. The knee pinning the coil is under the ochre tunic hem here, while in 9.4 v08 the cream dhoti shows at the knee. The staging matches the script. The rope has parted at a frayed end on the coil side of his hands, the free length slides through his open palms toward the rail and the spray at the right, his knee pins the coil, and the manacles are linked by their short chain. The two caption reserves sit top-left over the tunic and top-right over the rain and rigging, clear of the hands. Rejected: v01 to v07 all break the rope between his two hands. v04 to v06 also lack the knee and coil, v07's wrist cuffs are not linked, and v01 and v02 are 3:2.

Minor: the ladder in the hatch reads as intact, not clearly broken, and Nagoji is a medium-size figure rather than 'small' in the frame. Everything else matches: empty hatch with water pouring into the hold, nobody there, empty hinged collar with its ring, wrist chain, hobble chain, reddened open palms trailing bandage strips, and the frayed rope coil at his feet. Face matches the sheet (thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold stud). His left forearm is covered by the tunic sleeve. The top-right painted box sits over sky and rigging. The other candidates fail. v03 is the same art but with the left inner forearm bare and turned to camera, which breaks the hidden-brand rule. v01 and v02 also show the bare left forearm, and they put a loose bandage strip at his feet where the frayed rope coil should be.

v03 is clean. Tight rain-soaked face on the right: thick curled moustache, stubbled clean chin, gold stud, collar with ring, eyes turned right toward the off-panel hatch. On the left a ragged-edged dust memory shows Deccan riders galloping away with backs turned (anonymous), a saffron pennant with no marks, and a fallen comrade face down beside his fallen horse, with no blood. Both painted boxes sit on the memory, clear of the face. Small deviation: the horse lies down instead of standing riderless. Backup v07 has a standing riderless horse but carries painted black letterbox bars top and bottom that must be cropped out, and its riders are small silhouettes. v04, v05 and v06 fail the 'tight on face' framing (seated full figure). v01 and v02 repeat v03's art at 3:2 and would lose the face or the memory in a full-width crop.

v03: profile at the rail, facing out to sea. Two turns of rope round his chest pulled tight by bandaged, manacled hands, frayed free end trailing, empty collar with ring, joined wrist chain, and a ragged tunic flap and bandage over the far (left) forearm. The splintered, barnacled spar rides the foam. The hobble chain is out of frame because of the waist-up crop, and the spar sits mid-distance rather than directly below. There is open storm sky right of his face for the 'Forgive me' balloon. Rejected: v01 (Portuguese guards on deck, not in the beat), v04 (rope tied to the spar and a hauling pose), v05 (hands on the rail, no knotting), v06 (hands behind his back and no collar), v07 (confused staging with no rail between him and the sea).

v07 is the only candidate whose wrists stay joined by the short wrist chain. It also shows the hobble chain at the ankles, the collar, two turns of rope round his chest with the frayed end trailing, both forearms under tunic flap and bandage, lightning sky, black water, and the ship's rail behind him. Face matches (moustache, clean chin, small gold stud). Caveat: he leaps screen-left with the ship on the right, the reverse of 10.3 where he faces screen-right toward the sea. That break in screen direction is acceptable across the cut, but a horizontal flip would restore continuity if the page reads awkwardly (both forearms are covered, so a flip is safe for the brand rule). Rejected: v02 (arms flung wide, only one wrist chained, rope rising from behind his neck), v03, v04 and v05 (arms spread with separate chain stubs on each wrist, implying a broken wrist chain), v01 (guards reaching from the rail, arms spread), v06 (a wrist chain and ankle chain running back to the ship, a gold hoop at the neck).

v04: underwater just below the white foam of his entry, looking up past him. Collar with ring, gold stud, moustache and clean chin match. Joined manacles and fists at the bottom edge, rope knotted round his chest, and the rope's free end snakes up toward the barnacled, splintered spar without being tied to it. The ship's dark hull heels away beyond. Minor: at extreme zoom a few barnacles have hole patterns that faintly suggest faces, but at print size they read as barnacles. Rejected: v01 and v02 (rope lashed around the spar instead of a free end), v03 (collar drawn split in two floating pieces, rope ends on the spar, 3:2 format), v05 (no collar, reddish marks on the shoulders, spar reads as part of the hull).
